intelligence.human_view: Think of it like trying on a jacket: in the shop he said "make it bigger" — then he wore it, walked around in it, and said "actually, this fits fine." The later verdict, from wearing it, is the one that stands. The bigger-text round was dispatched on the first verdict; the captain decides whether it still runs, stands down, or narrows to the laptop view only — the note records the verdict, it does not dispatch.

intelligence.naya_view: A verdict given from wearing the thing beats a verdict given from describing it. The first order — small text quite a bit bigger — came from his memory of the page; the softened verdict came from his phone in his hand, on the page itself. That is why the later word stands: the phone is his seat, and the phone says the size is probably okay. The laptop caveat stays attached — almost a little small there — so the next round, if it runs at all, knows exactly where the remaining gap is. And the swap question stays open beside it: he wants to try swapping a slide out for an image or a video, and the button exists — a tiny round button in the top corner of each board, hidden unless signed in as a member — but he had not yet tried it signed-in when the log was flushed. His own test closes that question, not our claim.
